note: The two sets are nearly identical in content and share the same strengths (member sizes, plate and angle designations, key dimension strings) and the same weaknesses (vague 'component' entities, duplicated plate claims, and a dubious 'C3X6 quantity 1' claim). Set A's only unique claim is a plain W10X12 section claim, which is supported by the page. Set B's only unique claim adds the condition 'Structure South Elevation - Main' to a W10X12 section claim, and that condition appears nowhere in the page text or image, making it an invented qualifier. That single invented condition makes B slightly worse.
remarks: Both sets repeat the same plate size under two names ('Plate (PL)' and 'PL member') and use generic 'component' entities for dimension strings (6", 4", 1/4") that cannot be bound to a specific part from the text layer alone. The 'C3X6 | quantity | 1' claim in both sets appears to bind a detail/callout number to a quantity attribute. The 'TYP' condition attached to the 2'-4 1/2" length is questionable: in the text layer TYP is adjacent to 1/4" (likely a weld size), not to the length dimension.
